pl-l2d38c1-d1e108.summary: Turns to the will and its end.

pl-l2d38c1-d1e111.summary: States with Augustine that the will is known by its end to be right or wrong; the end of good will is beatitude, eternal life, God himself; of evil will, evil delight or something else in which the will should not rest.
claims: The will is judged by its end.

pl-l2d38c1-d1e114.summary: Notes the prophet's 'I have seen the end of all perfection; your command is exceedingly broad': charity is the end of all perfection, of all good will and action, to which every precept is referred.
claims: Charity is the end of every precept.

pl-l2d38c1-d1e118.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: all divine precepts are referred to charity, as 'the end of the precept is charity from a pure heart' (1 Tim 1:5); what is done from fear of punishment or carnal intention, not referred to love of God and neighbor, is not yet done as it should be.
claims: Acts not referred to charity are not done rightly.

pl-l2d38c1-d1e123.summary: Concludes that the right end of will or action is charity, which is God, as shown earlier.

pl-l2d38c1.summary: Turns to the will and its end. A will is known to be right or wrong by its end; the end of good will is beatitude, eternal life, God himself; of evil will, evil delight or something else in which the will should not rest. The end of all perfection is charity (Ps 118:96): Augustine says all divine precepts are referred to charity (1 Tim 1:5), and what is done from fear of punishment or a carnal intention, not referred to love of God and neighbor, is not yet done as it should be.
claims: The will is judged right or wrong by its end.
The end of good will is beatitude, eternal life, God.
The end of evil will is evil delight or something the will should not rest in.
All precepts are referred to charity.
Acts not referred to love of God and neighbor are not done rightly.
